construct: Decision-curve analysis evaluates whether using a prediction model improves clinical decisions compared with default strategies such as treat-all or treat-none. Net benefit weights true-positive benefit against false-positive harm according to a chosen threshold probability and is plotted across clinically relevant thresholds.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: When discrimination and calibration are similar, the remaining question is clinical utility across treatment thresholds relative to treat-all and treat-none strategies, which decision-curve analysis evaluates using net benefit.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: ROC analysis is a strong distractor because it compares model discrimination, but the stem states discrimination is already similar and asks about threshold-dependent clinical consequences.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only decision-curve analysis incorporates threshold probabilities and compares model-guided decisions with treat-all and treat-none strategies.
